title: What would actually happen if the Earth stopped spinning?
description:
At the equator the ground moves at about 1,670 km/h. Stop the Earth and the ground stops, but you, the air and the oceans don't. Stop it slowly and the oceans drain to the poles and a day lasts a year. Meanwhile Earth really is slowing down: by about 1.8 thousandths of a second per day, per century.

Sources:
- What happens if Earth stops rotating? — Astronomy magazine (Edward Herrick-Gleason, astronomy educator): https://www.astronomy.com/science/what-happens-if-earth-stops-rotating/
- What Would Happen If The Earth Suddenly Stopped Spinning? — IFLScience (Dr. Alfredo Carpineti): https://www.iflscience.com/editors-blog/what-would-happen-if-the-earth-suddenly-stopped-spinning/
- Earth Fact Sheet — NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (NSSDCA): https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html
- The thought experiment: What would happen if the Earth stopped spinning? — BBC Science Focus Magazine: https://www.sciencefocus.com/planet-earth/the-thought-experiment-what-would-happen-if-the-earth-stopped-spinning/
- Measurement of the Earth's rotation: 720 BC to AD 2015 (Proc. R. Soc. A 472: 20160404, 2016) — Stephenson, Morrison & Hohenkerk, Proceedings of the Royal Society A (open access via PubMed Central): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5247521/
- Ancient Astronomers' Records Assist Modern Scientists — Archaeology magazine (Archaeological Institute of America): https://archaeology.org/?p=5775

Labels: the polar-ocean map is a simplified model (BBC Science Focus; Esri's Witold Fraczek via IFLScience), drawn roughly; 'past 100°C' is BBC Science Focus's estimate; the 200 million years is our own sum at today's average rate (3,600 s / 0.0018 s per century = 2,000,000 centuries); the real rate fluctuates. The bulge on the page is exaggerated (the real difference is 21 km out of 6,378). Coastlines: Natural Earth (public domain). Simplified: a hypothetical, not a forecast.
